original_text:
If I were to start learning #python again for analytics, this is how I would prioritize topics for learning:

Week 1: Learning python basics + Control flow Statement
⏩ Syntax, data types, variables, and basic operations
⏩If-Else condition, For and While loop ,Functions

Week 2: Data structures and data manipulations
⏩Lists and dictionaries
⏩Working with Text Data

Week 3 &4: Data Analysis Libraries
⏩Reading from and writing to files (CSV, XLSX)
⏩Introduction to Numpy, Pandas & Matplotlib

Data Manipulations using pandas:
⏩Working with data frames and series
⏩Basic operations Filtering, Merging, Sorting, Aggregating data

Data Visualization using Matplotlib/Seaborn:
⏩Creating Histograms, Scatterplot, Charts (Line, Bar, Pie)

Now start building mini projects. [ Start with basic EDA and keep adding complexities with time]

I will deprioritize learning and implementing ML algo's at the start and focus more on basics initially.

Gaurav Agrawal

#analytics #python #datafam

ai_analysis.summary: The post proposes a four-week learning roadmap for Python analytics. It begins with syntax, data types, variables, basic operations, control flow, and functions, followed by lists, dictionaries, and text data. The third and fourth weeks cover CSV and XLSX file handling, introductory use of NumPy, pandas, and Matplotlib, pandas operations on DataFrames and Series, and visualization with Matplotlib and Seaborn. After learning the fundamentals, the recommendation is to build exploratory data analysis mini projects, increasing complexity over time while initially deprioritizing machine-learning algorithms.
subtopics: Syntax, data types, variables, and basic operations
Reading and writing CSV and XLSX files
Histograms, scatter plots, line charts, bar charts, and pie charts

interview_questions.question: Which Python fundamentals should an analytics beginner learn before moving to data-analysis libraries?
interview_questions.answer:
The fundamentals include syntax, data types, variables, and basic operations.
Control-flow skills include if-else conditions, for loops, and while loops.
Functions are also part of the recommended foundation.

interview_questions.question: How can pandas be used to perform basic data manipulations after reading CSV or XLSX data?
interview_questions.answer:
Python can read the CSV or XLSX file into a structure used for analysis.
The analysis can work with pandas DataFrames and Series.
Basic pandas operations can filter, merge, sort, and aggregate the data.
The result can be written back to a file when file output is required.

interview_questions.question: Which visualizations can an analytics beginner create with Matplotlib and Seaborn, and which basic analysis operations can support them?
interview_questions.answer:
The post explicitly names histograms, scatter plots, line charts, bar charts, and pie charts.
The data preparation can include filtering, merging, sorting, and aggregating data with pandas.
The visualizations can be used as part of exploratory data analysis mini projects.

interview_questions.question: How should a beginner progress from Python fundamentals to analytics projects while deciding when to introduce machine learning?
interview_questions.answer:
The learner should first cover Python basics, control flow, functions, and core data structures.
The learner should then study text data, file handling, NumPy, pandas, and visualization libraries.
After the fundamentals, the learner should build basic exploratory data analysis mini projects and increase complexity over time.
Machine-learning algorithms should be deprioritized until the analytics fundamentals are established.
